title: Stability and diagonal of an ind-etale algebra
statement:
The classes of ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] and ind-Zariski
maps are stable under base change, composition, and filtered colimits. An
ind-etale map is weakly etale. If $B,C$ are ind-etale over $A$, every
$A$-algebra map $B\to C$ is ind-etale. Weakly etale maps are stable under
composition and base change.

proof.text: Work with commutative rings and small filtered diagrams in a common universe. Call the finite building blocks over a ring R either etale R-algebras or finite products of principal localizations R_f. Both are finitely presented: R_f=R[t]/(ft-1), and a finite product is presented by finitely many orthogonal idempotents summing to 1 and presentations of its factors. Every principal localization is etale by the open-immersion clause of the cited composition node, and finite products are etale by the cited finite-product node (including the empty product, the zero ring). Thus an ind-Zariski presentation is also an ind-etale presentation. For either class, the cited finite-presentation factorization lemma and its converse criterion give: L has a filtered presentation by building blocks if and only if every map P\to L from a finitely presented R-algebra factors through a building block. Choose a set of representatives of the building blocks when applying the criterion.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: finite-presentation building blocks and the factorization criterion

proof.text: For R\to R\prime and L=\varinjlim_i L_i, the canonical map \varinjlim_i(R\prime\otimes_R L_i)\to R\prime\otimes_R L is an isomorphism. Explicitly, maps from either side to an R\prime-algebra Q are compatible families of R-algebra maps L_i\to Q: the tensor universal property and then the colimit universal property give the mutually inverse correspondences. Each etale building block stays etale by the cited base-change node. For Zariski blocks, R\prime\otimes_R\prod_{a=1}^n R_{f_a}\cong\prod_{a=1}^n R\prime_{\bar f_a}: the finite orthogonal idempotents split the tensor product, and in each factor adjoining an inverse to f_a is adjoining an inverse to its image. This includes n=0. These presentations prove arbitrary base-change stability for both classes.

Let R\to B\to C be ind-etale. Write B=\varinjlim_i B_i with B_i etale over R and C=\varinjlim_j C_j with C_j etale over B. Given a finitely presented R-algebra P and P\to C, factor it through C_j by the cited factorization lemma. The cited etale-algebra descent node supplies i and an etale B_i-algebra H with C_j\cong B\otimes_{B_i}H. The latter is the filtered colimit of B_k\otimes_{B_i}H over arrows i\to k: this follows by the tensor universal property as in step 2. Factor P\to C_j through one such term. That term is etale over B_k by base change and over R by composition, so P\to C factors through an etale R-algebra. The criterion in step 1 proves the ind-etale composition assertion. All scheme uses here are on spectra of rings; the descent node itself supplies an affine algebra H, so no affineness of a descended scheme is assumed.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: composition, using affine finite-data descent

proof.text: For ind-Zariski R\to B\to C, write B=\varinjlim_i B_i with B_i=\prod_a R_{f_{ia}}, and C as a filtered colimit of blocks C_j=\prod_{b=1}^{m_j}B_{g_{jb}}. A map P\to C from a finitely presented R-algebra factors through some C_j. Choose one common i representing all finitely many g_{jb} in B_i, using the cited elementwise colimit description. Put H=\prod_b(B_i)_{g_{jb,i}}. Its base change to B is C_j, and C_j=\varinjlim_{i\to k}\prod_b(B_k)_{g_{jb,k}} by the explicit finite-product/localization calculation in step 2. Factor P\to C_j through one such term. If g in a factor R_f is a/f^N, then (R_f)_g\cong R_{fa}: making f and g invertible is exactly making f and a invertible. Hence that term is a finite product of principal R-localizations, including zero factors and empty products. The criterion in step 1 proves ind-Zariski composition; neither the elements g nor the product components have been assumed to descend without choosing their representatives.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: explicit denominator and product descent for ind-Zariski composition

proof.text: Let L=\varinjlim_i L_i with every L_i ind-etale, or with every L_i ind-Zariski, over a fixed R. Given finitely presented P and P\to L, the cited factorization lemma first factors it through L_i, and then through a finite building block in a chosen presentation of L_i. The criterion in step 1 gives a filtered presentation of L by building blocks of the same class. This proves the filtered-colimit assertion without imposing any compatibility between independently chosen presentations of the L_i. If the colimit assertion is read for a filtered diagram of arrows R_i\to L_i with varying bases, apply step 2 to R_i\to R=\varinjlim_i R_i. Then \varinjlim_i(R\otimes_{R_i}L_i)\cong\varinjlim_i L_i as R-algebras: maps out of either side are precisely compatible maps out of the L_i agreeing with the R_i structural maps.

Let B=\varinjlim_i E_i be ind-etale over A and put S=B\otimes_A B, with multiplication \mu:S\to B. For each i, E_i\otimes_A E_i is etale over E_i through its first factor by base change. Its multiplication is an E_i-algebra retraction. Apply the cited etale-section idempotent splitting node to obtain an idempotent e_i with \ker(\mu_i)=(1-e_i)(E_i\otimes_A E_i). Every element x of S has a representative x_i in some E_i\otimes_A E_i: write x as a finite sum of pure tensors and advance their finitely many coefficients to a common stage. If \mu(x)=0, the cited elementwise equality criterion gives an arrow i\to k where \mu_k(x_k)=0. Thus x is a multiple of the image of 1-e_k. Conversely those images all lie in \ker\mu. Consequently \ker\mu is generated by idempotents, with no compatibility required among the chosen e_i.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: finite etale diagonals and their kernel in the colimit

proof.text: Write J=\ker\mu, generated by idempotents q_\alpha as proved in step 6, and let U be the multiplicative subset of S generated by 1-q_\alpha. The quotient S/J inverts U since each 1-q_\alpha maps to 1. In U^{-1}S each q_\alpha vanishes because q_\alpha(1-q_\alpha)=0 and 1-q_\alpha is invertible. The quotient and localization universal properties give inverse maps S/J\leftrightarrows U^{-1}S fixing every element of S. Multiplication is surjective (b=\mu(b\otimes1)), hence B\cong S/J\cong U^{-1}S. For finite subsets F of the generators, invert u_F=\prod_{\alpha\in F}(1-q_\alpha); these principal localizations form a filtered presentation of U^{-1}S, since any map inverting all u_F inverts precisely U. Thus \mu is ind-Zariski. Each principal localization S_{u_F} is flat over S by the cited localization-flat node, and applying the cited filtered-colimit-flat-modules node to this filtered presentation shows that \mu is flat as an S-module. Each E_i is flat over A by the definition of etale and the affine flatness equivalence. To see the underlying A-module of B is their filtered module colimit, take the disjoint union of stage modules modulo eventual equality: the cited ring-colimit description gives the same set and the same addition and A-scalar multiplication. The cited filtered-colimit-flat-modules node therefore makes B flat over A. Together these two flatness assertions prove weak etaleness.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: localization of the diagonal and flatness

proof.text: For an A-algebra map h:B\to C between ind-etale A-algebras, factor it as b\mapsto b\otimes1 from B to B\otimes_A C, followed by p(b\otimes c)=h(b)c. The first map is the base change of A\to C and is ind-etale by step 2. The second is a base change of \mu_B:B\otimes_A B\to B from step 7 along \theta:B\otimes_A B\to B\otimes_A C, \theta(b_1\otimes b_2)=b_1\otimes h(b_2). The pushout isomorphism (B\otimes_A C)\otimes_{B\otimes_A B} B\cong C sends (b\otimes c)\otimes b\prime to h(bb\prime)c, with inverse c\mapsto(1\otimes c)\otimes1. Balancing moves b\prime to the first tensor factor and then uses b\otimes1=1\otimes h(b), verifying both inverse identities. Under this isomorphism the base-changed multiplication is exactly p. By ind-Zariski base-change stability, p is ind-Zariski, hence ind-etale by step 1. Ind-etale composition from step 3 now proves h ind-etale.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: the relative assertion, with the actual pushout maps

proof.text: For weakly etale A\to B\to C, A\to C is flat by the cited flat-composition node. Its multiplication factors as C\otimes_A C\to C\otimes_B C\to C. The first arrow is the base change of \mu_B along B\otimes_A B\to C\otimes_A C, b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto b_1\otimes b_2: explicitly (C\otimes_A C)\otimes_{B\otimes_A B}B\cong C\otimes_B C via (c_1\otimes c_2)\otimes b\mapsto bc_1\otimes c_2. The inverse takes c_1\otimes_B c_2 to (c_1\otimes_A c_2)\otimes1, which is B-balanced by the tensor relations. The first arrow is flat by flat module base change and the second by weak etaleness of B\to C; composition makes \mu_{C/A} flat. For A\to A\prime and B\prime=A\prime\otimes_A B, the structural map A\prime\to B\prime is flat by base change. Its diagonal satisfies B\prime\otimes_{A\prime}B\prime\cong A\prime\otimes_A(B\otimes_A B); under the associativity isomorphism its multiplication is the base change of \mu_B, hence flat by the same base-change node. This proves both remaining weak-etale stability assertions.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: weak-etale composition and base change
